london_system.name: London System
london_system.summary: A solid, easy-to-learn opening. You play the same setup almost every game. Bishop out before e3 — that's the golden rule.
golden_rules: Bishop to f4 first, before e3. Always.
Don't trade your dark bishop unless you get something big.
Your dream setup: d4, e3, Bf4, Nf3, Bd3, O-O.
After setup is done, push for e4.

traps.name: Englund Gambit Trap
traps.description: They play 1...e5 trying to trick you. Take the pawn and win.
traps.trap_idea: They try to grab your b2 pawn with their queen. Let them — then trap the queen.
traps.how_to_avoid: Just play normal development. Their queen gets stuck.

traps.name: Bg4 Pin Trick
traps.description: They pin your knight spot with Bg4. You have a strong response.
traps.trap_idea: Push h3 then g4 to kick their bishop, then jump Ne5.
traps.how_to_avoid: Don't panic when they play Bg4. h3 then g4 is strong.

traps.name: Queen Trap after c5
traps.description: They take b2 with their queen. Nb5 and Rb1 traps it.
traps.trap_idea: Let them take b2. Their queen has no escape.
traps.how_to_avoid: Make sure you have Nb5 before allowing Qxb2.

d4.hint: What's the strongest first move to grab the center?
d4.right_feedback: Good — d4 grabs the center. Now think about your bishop.

d5.name: Main Line
d5.idea_opponent: They take their share of the center. Fair game.
d5.hint: Which piece should come out BEFORE you play e3?
d5.right_feedback: Exactly — Bf4 before e3. Golden rule of the London.
d5.wrong_feedback: In the London, the bishop MUST come to f4 before e3.

Nf6.name: Indian Setup
Nf6.hint: Same question as always — which piece first?
Nf6.right_feedback: Bf4 — doesn't matter what they play, bishop first.

c5.name: Early c5
c5.hint: They attacked your center. What's the calm response?
c5.right_feedback: e3 — stay calm. Your center holds.

Qb6.hint: Their queen eyes b2. How do you develop AND set a trap?
Qb6.right_feedback: Nc3 — if they take b2, Nb5+Rb1 traps their queen.

e5.name: Englund Gambit
e5.idea_opponent: A trick! They sacrifice a pawn hoping you blunder.
e5.hint: They offered a pawn. Should you take it?
e5.right_feedback: Take it. The Englund Gambit is bad for Black if you play correctly.
e5.wrong_feedback: Take the pawn! dxe5 is strong.

Bf5.name: Mirror London
Bf5.hint: They mirrored your London. Change your plan?
Bf5.right_feedback: e3 — stick to the plan. You have more space.

when_ahead.plan: Push e4 to open the center. Trade off defensive pieces.
ideas: Knight on e5 is a monster

when_equal.plan: Aim for e4. If blocked, play on the queenside with a4-a5.

when_behind.plan: Keep it closed. d4+e3 is hard to break. Wait for their mistake.

endgame_tips: d4+e3 structure is solid in endgames.
Activate your king early.
Push passed pawns.

italian_game.name: Italian Game
italian_game.summary: A classic opening. Develop quickly, point your bishop at f7, and attack the king. Simple and dangerous.
golden_rules: Bishop to c4 — aim at f7, the weakest square.
c3 prepares d4 — the ideal center.
Castle before attacking.
Don't grab pawns if it loses time.

traps.name: Fried Liver Attack
traps.description: Knight goes to g5 attacking f7. If they take, you sacrifice the knight for a devastating attack.
traps.trap_idea: After Nxf7, their king is dragged out. The attack is crushing.
traps.how_to_avoid: Black should play d5 instead of allowing Ng5.

traps.name: Legal's Mate
traps.description: Sacrifice the queen to deliver checkmate with minor pieces.
traps.trap_idea: If they take your queen with Bxd1, you play Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5#. Checkmate!
traps.how_to_avoid: Don't take the queen if you see Bxf7+ coming.

traps.name: Blackburne Shilling Gambit
traps.description: Black plays Nd4 hoping you grab f7. Don't — just take the knight.
traps.trap_idea: Bxf7+ looks tempting but wastes your bishop. Nxd4 wins a piece.
traps.how_to_avoid: Don't be greedy. Nxd4 is simple and strong.

e4.idea: Control the center and open lines for your bishop.
e4.hint: What's the most popular opening move in chess?
e4.right_feedback: e4 — king's pawn opening. Controls the center and frees your bishop.

e5.name: Open Game
e5.idea_opponent: They mirror your center pawn. Classic response.
e5.hint: Develop a piece that also attacks their e5 pawn.
e5.right_feedback: Nf3 — develops AND attacks e5. Two jobs in one move.

Nc6.name: Italian Setup
Nc6.idea_opponent: Defending e5 with the knight. Standard.
Nc6.hint: Where should your bishop go to create the most pressure?
Nc6.right_feedback: Bc4 — aimed at f7, the weakest square in their position.
Nc6.wrong_feedback: Bc4 targets f7 — the weak spot next to their king.

Bc5.name: Giuoco Piano
Bc5.hint: How do you prepare to build an ideal center with d4?

Nf6.name: Two Knights Defense
Nf6.hint: Their knight attacks e4. But f7 is weak. What aggressive move targets it?
Nf6.right_feedback: Ng5 — threatening Nxf7! This is the Fried Liver territory.
Nf6.wrong_feedback: Ng5 attacks f7 with two pieces. Very dangerous for Black.

d5.name: Main Defense
d5.idea_opponent: The correct defense — counter in the center.
d5.right_feedback: exd5 — now you have an extra pawn in the center.

Bc5.name: Traxler Counter
Bc5.idea_opponent: They ignore f7 and counter-attack your f2.
Bc5.hint: They left f7 undefended! Take it?
Bc5.right_feedback: Nxf7 — fork the queen and rook!

Nd4.name: Blackburne Shilling
Nd4.idea_opponent: A trick! They want you to grab f7.
Nd4.hint: Their knight jumped to d4. Bxf7+ looks tempting. But is there something simpler?
Nd4.right_feedback: Nxd4 — just take the knight! Don't be greedy with Bxf7+.
Nd4.wrong_feedback: Bxf7+ wastes your strong bishop. Nxd4 wins a piece for free.

when_ahead.plan: Open the center with d4. Attack the king.

when_equal.plan: Control d4 and d5. Keep bishops active.

when_behind.plan: Keep pieces active. Look for tactical tricks.
ideas: Don't trade into a bad endgame

endgame_tips: Bishop pair is strong in open endgames.
Central pawns are powerful.
Activate rooks on open files.

italian_game_black.name: Italian Game (Black side)
italian_game_black.summary: White plays the Italian. As Black, develop solidly, watch for f7 tricks, and counter in the center with d5.
golden_rules: Watch f7 — it's your weakest square.
d5 counter-strike is your best weapon.
Don't let White build a perfect center with d4.
Castle early — your king needs safety.

traps.name: Traxler Counterattack
traps.description: Instead of defending f7, counter-attack their f2! Dangerous for White.
traps.trap_idea: White expects you to defend. Bc5 attacks f2 and creates chaos.
traps.how_to_avoid: White should be careful — Bc5 is a real counter.

e4.hint: White played e4. What's the most natural response to fight for the center?
e4.right_feedback: e5 — fight for the center. Classic.

e5.name: Open Game
e5.idea_opponent: You take your share of the center.

when_ahead.plan: Push d5 to open the center. Use your active pieces.

when_equal.plan: Play d5 when ready. Keep pieces active.
ideas: Don't let White dominate the center

when_behind.plan: Keep it closed. Look for counter-chances on the kingside.
ideas: Don't trade into a lost endgame

endgame_tips: Central pawns matter.
Activate your king quickly.
Rooks belong on open files.

sicilian_defense.name: Sicilian Defense
sicilian_defense.summary: The sharpest response to e4. You fight for the center with c5 instead of e5. Leads to rich, complex positions.
golden_rules: c5 fights for d4 without committing your e-pawn.
You're playing for a queenside counter-attack.
Don't be scared of White's kingside attack — you attack queenside.
d6 + Nf6 is the solid setup.

traps.name: Siberian Trap
traps.description: Black plays Qa5 pinning the knight and threatening Bxc3+.
traps.trap_idea: White's knight on c3 is pinned. If they don't see it, you win material.
traps.how_to_avoid: White should play Bd2 or Nb3 to break the pin.

traps.name: Magnus Smith Trap
traps.description: White plays Bc4 and after Bg7, Nd5! forks everything.
traps.trap_idea: The knight on d5 attacks multiple pieces. Black's in trouble.
traps.how_to_avoid: Black should delay Bg7 and play a6 or e6 first.

e4.hint: White played e4. Instead of e5, what move fights for d4 from the side?
e4.right_feedback: c5 — the Sicilian! You fight for the center without copying White.

c5.name: Sicilian Defense
c5.idea_opponent: You challenge d4 from the flank.

when_ahead.plan: Push on the queenside with a5-a4, b5-b4. Open the a and b files.
ideas: Your bishops are strong on long diagonals

when_equal.plan: Control d5 and fight for the center.
ideas: Knights on c6 and d4 are strong

when_behind.plan: Complicate. The Sicilian is a fighting opening.

endgame_tips: Your queenside pawns can be dangerous.
The Sicilian often leads to opposite-side attacks.
King activity is key.

caro_kann.name: Caro-Kann Defense
caro_kann.summary: A solid, reliable response to e4. You play c6 then d5, challenging the center while keeping a solid pawn structure.
golden_rules: c6 then d5 — challenge the center solidly.
Get your bishop OUT before playing e6 (same idea as London!).
Your pawn structure is your strength.
Don't rush — the Caro-Kann is about patience.

traps.name: Caro-Kann Smothered Mate
traps.description: White plays Nd6# — smothered mate! Black's pieces block all escape squares.
traps.trap_idea: The knight on d6 delivers checkmate because Black's own pieces block the king.
traps.how_to_avoid: Black should not play Nd7 and Ngf6 without checking for Nd6.

e4.hint: White played e4. What move prepares d5 while keeping your structure solid?
e4.right_feedback: c6 — prepares d5. Solid and reliable.

when_ahead.plan: Use your solid structure. Push pawns on the queenside.
ideas: Rooks on c and d files

when_equal.plan: Stay solid. The Caro-Kann is a fortress.
ideas: Knights on d5 or e4 outposts

when_behind.plan: Keep the position closed. Your structure is hard to break.

endgame_tips: Your pawn structure shines in endgames.
Bishop + pawns endgames favor you.
Passed c-pawn can be a winner.

french_defense.name: French Defense
french_defense.summary: Play e6 then d5. You let White take space but build a solid wall and counter-attack later.
golden_rules: e6 first, then d5 — challenge the center.
Your light bishop gets locked in. Find a way to activate it.
c5 is your key counter-strike against d4.
Be patient — the French is a slow burn.

traps.name: French Winawer Poisoned Pawn
traps.description: Black grabs the g2 pawn with Qg4. Risky but powerful if White doesn't know the theory.
traps.trap_idea: The g2 pawn is free and White's kingside is weak.
traps.how_to_avoid: White should protect g2 or play Qg4 prevention lines.

e4.hint: White played e4. What move builds a wall and prepares d5?
e4.right_feedback: e6 — the French Defense. Solid wall, then strike with d5.

when_ahead.plan: Break with c5 and open the position for your pieces.

when_equal.plan: Play c5 and look to free your light bishop.

when_behind.plan: Keep it closed. Your pawn chain is hard to break.

endgame_tips: Your pawn structure is solid.
The bad bishop problem disappears in endgames with trades.
King activity matters.

queens_gambit.name: Queen's Gambit
queens_gambit.summary: Offer a pawn with c4 to control the center. If they take, you get it back easily. Classic, strong, reliable.
golden_rules: c4 fights for d5 control.
If they take c4, don't panic — you get it back.
Bg5 pins the knight — classic pressure.
Control d5, then attack.

traps.name: Elephant Trap
traps.description: White takes d5 thinking it wins a pawn. But Nxe4! wins the bishop because of the pin.
traps.trap_idea: After Nxe4, White's bishop on g5 is attacked by the queen, and the knight on e4 forks.
traps.how_to_avoid: White should NOT play Nxd5 in this position.

d4.hint: Start with center control. What's the move?

d5.name: QGD
d5.hint: How do you challenge their d5 pawn?
d5.right_feedback: c4 — the Queen's Gambit! Attack their center.

dxc4.name: QGA
dxc4.idea_opponent: They took the pawn. You'll get it back.
dxc4.hint: How do you recapture the c4 pawn?
dxc4.right_feedback: e3 — opens the bishop to take back on c4.

when_ahead.plan: Push e4 and open the center. Your pieces are better.
ideas: Push b4-b5 on the queenside to crack their pawns
Rooks on c and d files

when_equal.plan: Hold d5. Push b4-b5 to break their queenside pawn structure.

when_behind.plan: Simplify. Your pawn structure is usually good.
ideas: Don't let them attack your king

endgame_tips: Central pawns are strong.
Pushing b4-b5 on the queenside cracks their pawn structure and creates weak squares to land pieces on.
Rook endgames favor better structure.

scandinavian_defense.name: Scandinavian Defense
scandinavian_defense.summary: Immediately challenge e4 with d5. Simple, direct, and gets your queen active early.
golden_rules: Take the pawn back with your queen — Qd5 or Qd6.
Get your bishop out before e6 — same as London.
Qa5 is the safest queen square.
Develop quickly — your queen is already out.

traps.name: Portuguese Gambit Trap
traps.description: Instead of taking back the pawn, play Nf6 then Bg4, creating tactical pressure.
traps.trap_idea: Bg4 pins the queen to the king. If White plays Be2, Nxd5 wins the pawn back with activity.
traps.how_to_avoid: White should be careful about the pin and not play passively.

e4.hint: White played e4. How do you immediately challenge it?
e4.right_feedback: d5 — strike the center right away! That's the Scandinavian.

when_ahead.plan: Your development lead matters. Open lines.

when_equal.plan: Solid development. Bf5, e6, c6 fortress.

when_behind.plan: Keep it solid. Your pawn structure is reliable.

endgame_tips: Your structure is solid.
Active queen gives endgame chances.
Don't let them control the d-file.

ruy_lopez.name: Ruy Lopez
ruy_lopez.summary: The king of openings. Bb5 puts pressure on Black's defense of e5. Deep, strategic, tested for centuries.
golden_rules: Bb5 doesn't try to WIN the e5 pawn — it puts long-term pressure.
Castle early, then build with c3+d4.
Re1 supports e4 and puts pressure on the e-file.
Be patient — the Ruy Lopez is a marathon, not a sprint.

traps.name: Noah's Ark Trap
traps.description: Black traps White's bishop on b3 with a5-a4. The bishop has nowhere to go.
traps.trap_idea: After a5, a4, the bishop is trapped by its own pawns.
traps.how_to_avoid: White should retreat the bishop to d5 or c2 early.

e5.name: Open Game
e5.right_feedback: Nf3 — two birds with one stone.

Nc6.name: Ruy Lopez
Nc6.hint: Where does the bishop go to put pressure on their e5 defense?
Nc6.right_feedback: Bb5 — the Ruy Lopez! Pressure on Nc6 which defends e5.
Nc6.wrong_feedback: Bb5 puts indirect pressure on e5 through the Nc6 defender.

a6.name: Morphy Defense
a6.hint: They kicked your bishop. Where does it retreat to stay active?
a6.right_feedback: Ba4 — stays on the diagonal, still eyeing c6.

Nf6.name: Berlin Defense
Nf6.hint: Your e4 is attacked. But castling first is more important. Why?
Nf6.right_feedback: O-O — king safety first. e4 isn't really hanging because of the pin.

when_ahead.plan: Push d4 and open the center.

when_equal.plan: Build slowly with c3, d4, Nbd2-f1-g3.
ideas: Maneuver knight to g3 or f5

when_behind.plan: Keep pieces active. The Ruy Lopez structure is resilient.

endgame_tips: The Ruy Lopez often leads to complex endgames.
Bishop pair is an advantage.
Central control wins endgames.

scotch_game.name: Scotch Game
scotch_game.summary: Open the center on move three. Sharper than the Italian. Trade in the middle and push the d-pawn.
golden_rules: d4 on move three — fight for the center immediately.
Trade in the centre, develop, then push.
Don't fear early queen trades — your pieces are more active.
Watch for c-file pressure and the Nf5 jump.

when_ahead.plan: Trade pieces. The d-pawn becomes a monster.

when_equal.plan: Keep pieces active. Look for c-file or e-file pressure.

when_behind.plan: Stay sharp. Avoid trades into a worse endgame.

endgame_tips: An advanced d-pawn is a winning weapon.
Bishop pair is strong with open files.
Centralise rooks before pushing.

petrov_defense.name: Petrov Defense
petrov_defense.summary: Mirror White's knight. The most solid answer to 1.e4 e5 — equalise and grind.
golden_rules: Nf6 mirrors White's knight — symmetric and solid.
After Nxe5, retreat with d6 first, then take on e4.
Play d5 to anchor your central knight.
Trade favourably — solid endgames are your friend.

when_equal.plan: Develop, castle, keep the position simple.

when_behind.plan: Hold the centre. Don't let pieces get pushed back.

endgame_tips: Symmetric pawn endgames usually draw — that's often fine.
Active rook beats a passive bishop.
Keep your king centralised in the endgame.

kings_indian_defense.name: King's Indian Defense
kings_indian_defense.summary: Let White build a big centre, then smash it. Fianchetto, castle, push f5 and attack.
golden_rules: Fianchetto the bishop to g7 — long diagonal at the queenside.
Castle early, attack later. Safety first.
Push e5 (or c5) to challenge the centre.
When White locks the centre, your f5 break is the main plan.

when_ahead.plan: Convert the kingside attack — pawns roll forward.

when_equal.plan: Build the kingside attack patiently. Trade only if it helps the attack.
ideas: Reroute the knight to f4 or h5

when_behind.plan: Activate pieces. The dark bishop is your soul.

endgame_tips: The dark-square bishop is worth more than a passive rook.
King centralisation matters — use yours.
Passed pawns on the kingside can decide.

nimzo_indian_defense.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
nimzo_indian_defense.summary: Pin White's c3 knight on move three. Cripple their pawns, take the bishop pair, play solid.
golden_rules: Bb4 pins the c3 knight — main idea of the opening.
Aim to trade your bishop for the knight, doubling White's c-pawns.
Castle, then play d5 or c5 to challenge the centre.
After Bxc3+, develop the queen bishop on b7 or e6.

when_ahead.plan: Exploit doubled c-pawns. Pressure them and trade.

when_equal.plan: Solid structure. Look for the right pawn break.
ideas: Knight reroute to e4 or g4

when_behind.plan: Stay solid. Don't open the position for White's bishops.

endgame_tips: Doubled isolated c-pawns are a long-term weakness — target them.
Knight beats bishop in closed endgames.
Active king in the endgame is worth a pawn.

slav_defense.name: Slav Defense
slav_defense.summary: Support d5 with c6 instead of e6. Keeps the queen bishop free. Solid and respectable.
golden_rules: c6 holds d5 without locking in the bishop.
Develop the queen bishop OUTSIDE the pawn chain — to f5 or g4.
After dxc4, hold the pawn with b5 if you can.
Don't rush e6 — keep options open.

when_ahead.plan: Trade favourably. Solid pawn structure converts.

when_equal.plan: Develop calmly. Look for e5 or c5 breaks.

when_behind.plan: Stay solid. Slav is hard to crack.

endgame_tips: Solid pawns convert small advantages.
Bishop pair shines in open positions.
Centralise your king in the endgame.

english_opening.name: English Opening
english_opening.summary: Start with c4. Control d5 from a distance. Calm positional play, often with a fianchetto.
golden_rules: c4 controls d5 — no rush to push pawns in the centre.
Fianchetto the bishop to g2 — long diagonal at the queenside.
Develop knights to c3 and f3 before committing the centre.
Pawn breaks come later: e4, d4, or even b4.

when_equal.plan: Manoeuvre patiently. Look for the right break.
ideas: d4 or e4 at the right moment

when_behind.plan: Stay flexible. The English is hard to attack.

endgame_tips: The fianchettoed bishop is your best endgame piece.
Knight outposts on d5 or e4 are killer.
Queenside majority converts to a passed pawn.

modern_defense.name: Modern Defense (Classical Setup)
modern_defense.summary: How to handle Black's Modern Defense (1...g6). Take the center with e4 + d4, develop Bc4 + Nf3 + O-O, push e5 to claim space, then ALWAYS support d4 with c3 — never Nbc3, which blocks the supporting pawn.
golden_rules: After d4 + e5, support the center with c3 — not Nbc3.
Nbc3 blocks the c-pawn permanently. The c-pawn needs c3 to support d4.
Develop Bc4 + Nf3 + O-O before pushing e5.
Black's Nc6 puts pressure on d4 — c3 is the structural answer.
After c3, plan Nbd2 + Bd3 / Bb3 + Re1 to complete development.

e4.right_feedback: Good — e4 grabs the center against the Modern.

g6.name: Modern Defense
g6.idea_opponent: Black fianchettos, will pressure your center from the flank.
g6.hint: Claim more space with the queen's pawn?
g6.right_feedback: Right — d4 gives you the big center.

Bg7.name: Fianchetto
Bg7.idea_opponent: Bishop aims at your d4-e5 chain.
Bg7.right_feedback: Bc4 — bishop on the long diagonal toward f7.

e6.name: Hybrid Setup with ...e6
e6.idea_opponent: Black solidifies the dark squares around the fianchetto.
e6.hint: Develop the knight, defend d4 indirectly.
e6.right_feedback: Nf3 — protects d4 from any future ...e5 / ...c5 break.

Nc6.name: Knight attacks d4
Nc6.idea_opponent: Black's knight presses on your d4 pawn.
Nc6.hint: Get the king safe before pushing forward.

Ne7.name: Knight reroute
Ne7.hint: Claim the e5 square — clamp the center.
Ne7.right_feedback: e5 — big center, Black's knight on e7 is now passive.

a6.name: Queenside prep
a6.idea_opponent: Black prepares ...b5 to harass your Bc4.
a6.hint: In the Modern Defense, Black's knight on c6 attacks your d4. How do you defend d4 without blocking your own pawn?
a6.right_feedback: In the Modern Defense, c3 supports your d4 pawn — keeps the big center solid. Your b1-knight can come to d2 next.
a6.wrong_feedback: In the Modern Defense, the idea is: c3 (the pawn) supports your d4 + e5 center. Nc3 blocks the c-pawn for good — now d4 has no pawn behind it. Black plays ...d6 then ...dxe5 and your big center falls apart.

middlegame_plans: After c3 + Nbd2, expand with Bd3 (or Bb3) + Re1 + h3 + a4 — patient development.
Watch for Black's ...d6 / ...d5 break — meet ...d5 with exd6 e.p. when available.
Trade Black's fianchetto bishop if you can win a tempo doing it.
endgame_tips: Your d4-e5 chain becomes a queenside majority in pawn endings — push the queenside.
Black's dark-square bishop is the key piece; trade it for any meaningful concession.
